 BEFORE: HONBLE MEMBER :

MEMBER : Sri. Shankar Coari.
FOR COMPLAINANT : Sri Barun Prasad,
Advocate.
FOR THE OPPOSITE PARTIES

Member.
1. This complaint has been filed
u/s 17
read with
section 13
and
14
of
the Consumer Protection Act 1986, against the OPs praying for direction upon
the OPs for an order either to replace 56 defective LCD 17 inch monitors by a
new one or to refund the entire price of Rs.10,54,560/- along with interest
@12% p.a. from the date of payment till realization, compensation to the tune
of Rs.25,00,000/- due to gross deficiency in service, harassment, loss of
goodwill reputation and faith among the students, Rs.10,000/- towards
litigation cost to the Complainant. In the complaint petition the Complainant
alleged deficiency in service and defectiveness in the goods supplied by the
OPs, purchased by the Complainant.
2. The brief facts of the Complainant as stated in the complaint
petition are that the Complainant is a non-profitable and charitable
organization and a society registered under the
Registration of Society Act
XXI
of 1860. The Complainant runs one school in the name of Sri Jain Vidyalaya and
for the purpose of betterment of its students education the Complainant
intended to purchase 30 numbers of Dell Desktop and 30 numbers of 17 inch LCD
Monitors (DELL) and therefore approached the OP-2 who is the sales
representative of the OP-1 (the manufacturer of DELL computers and LCD
monitors) in the month of July 2008 and the OP-2 issued one offer and its rate
chart for the same. As per the offer made by the OP-2 the Complainant-
institution purchased 30 DELL Desktop and 30 numbers of 17 inch LCD Monitors
(DELL) from the OP-2 on 07.08.2008 vide a invoice dated 07.08.2008 and paid an
amount of Rs.10,54,560/- including VAT @4%. The Complainant also exchanged 30
existing monitors of DELL from the OP-2. All the Computers have been installed
in the said Vidlayay of the Complainant- Institution but from the very
beginning of installation total 60 in numbers became defective along with
several spots on the screen. All the monitors were almost in a bad condition
and therefore lying unused due to several problems. The OPs provided the
Complainant three years warranty for all the purchased items. As the defects in
all the monitors occurred within the warranty period the Complainant
immediately intimated the defects to the OP-2 from whom items were purchased
and thereafter several e-mail correspondences were made with the OP-2 & 3
for the purpose of repairing of the defective DELL 17 inch LCD monitors on
02.12.2008. In response to all the Complainants made by the Complainant with
the OP-2 and 3 for replacement of defective monitors the OP-2 & 3 also
started regular correspondences with the OP-1- the manufacturer of those
monitors. The Complainant has mentioned that after receiving complaint from the
petition the OP2 as well as OP-3 visited the school and inspected the
monitors, found those monitors as defective which they also conveyed to the
manufacturer-OP-1 and suggested for replacement of those monitors as early as
possible. One service engineer namely Sri Atanu Roy came to the school of the
Petitioners on 03.12.2008 and inspected DELL 17 inch LCD monitors 60 in numbers
and observed lots of black spot on the screen. The OP-2 through e-mail dated
04.12.2008 requested the OP-1 for replacement of all the 60 monitors because
all were defective. The OP-1 and 3 acknowledged the same and intimated to send
their mechanic for taking photographs of all the monitors and they also agreed
to replace all the 60 defective monitors with a new one. After several complaints
made by the Complainant before the OPs, the OPs send their mechanic for
replacement of only 04 LCD monitors out of 60 LCD monitors on 23.12.2008.
Thereafter, the OPs did not replace the rest 56 LCD monitors to the Complainant
in spite of repeated request. Ultimately the Complainant wrote one letter-dated
24.01.2009 to the OPs with a request to replace all the defective LCD monitors
on or before 10.02.2009. The OP-3 by their letter dated 20.02.2009 intimated
the OP-1 that due to their delay in replacement of all the defective monitors
the customer suffered a lot and made them liable for the situation and further
requested to take serious action in this matter to solve the issue. In reply to
the letter of the OP-3 the OP-1 through their e-mail on 20.03.2009 intimated
that after obtaining samples of 2 monitors they referred the same to LG Koria
for analysis who opined that due to humidity and customer operation condition
of the panels is irreparable and the same defects occurred in all the monitors
and therefore, replacement of 60 LCD monitors is more costlier than a new one
and therefore the OP-1 denied to replace all the defective 60 monitors of the
Complainant. The Complainant has mentioned in the petition of complaint that
the OP-1 just to avoid their liability of replacement of defective monitors
shifted their liability to the shoulder of the Petitioners with some false and
baseless allegation, which has no base at all. The OPs admitted the defects in
all the 60 monitors within its warranty and therefore they are duty bound to
replace and/or refund the entire cost price of all the monitors along with
interest and compensation. That due to manufacturing defects in all the 60
monitors and clear admission by the OPs about the defects and thereafter denial
to replace the same tantamount to gross deficiency in service on their part and
thus the OPs are liable either to replace the defective LCD monitors or refund
the entire price paid by the Complainant for purchase of those monitors along
with interest @ 12% p.a. The Complainant being a charitable institution and for
the purpose of educational development of their students purchased those LCD
monitors just to teach and give better knowledge to the students but due to
defects in all the monitors the entire education system hampered and students
missed their opportunity to learn computer from this institution and thereafter
the Complainant has suffered huge loss of good will, reputation and faith from
their students. Under the above circumstances the Complainant has to come up
before the Ld. Forum for getting necessary orders directing the OPs either to
replace all the defective monitors in default refund the entire purchase price
to the Complainant along with interest, compensation and litigation cost.
3. The OP-1 has contested the petition of complaint by filing written
version wherein it is stated that the instant complaint is neither maintainable
nor on facts and this Commission has no jurisdiction to adjudicate the
complaint, so the Complainant is liable to be rejected in limine. The OP-1 has
stated that the Complainant purchased monitors to be used by its students in
its school; therefore, the Complainant does not fall under the definition of
consumer as per
Consumer Protection Act
. And for this reason the Complainant
cannot be allowed to agitate its grievance before this Commission. It has been
contended the OP 1 regarding allegation of deficiency in service and unfair
trade practice on behalf of the OP-1 that DELL Desktops and 17 inch LCD
Monitors were purchased and 30 Monitors exchanged by the Complainants monitors
were part of a larger consignment sold by the OP-1 to the OP-3. The consignment
was shift to the OP-3 from the OP-1 on 27.03.2008. Thereafter the OP-3 sold the
Desktops and Monitors to the OP-2 who in turned sold it to the Complainant on
07.08.2008. The OP-1 has submitted that the monitors and the desktops were sold
to the Complainant after about five months from the date of initial shipment by
the OP-1 to the OP-3. As on the date of purchase by the complainant the
monitors and desktops were with the OP-2 and/or OP-3 for over five months, when
the monitor and Desktops were dispatched by the OP-1, the said articles were in
good working condition and had no defect in respect of manufacturing or otherwise.
It has been submitted by the OP-1 that the OP-2 contacted the OP-1s technical
support on 02.12.2008 and reported that Complainant has noticed a few black
spots on the monitors purchased by it. The OP-1s technical support personnel
immediately recorded the complainant and made arrangements for his senior
service engineer to visit the Petitioner and examine the said monitors in this
regard. A service engineer visited the Complainant on 03.12.2008, examined the
monitors and confirmed the visibility of black spot on the monitors. The OP-1s
technical support team communicated the same to the OP-2 and took 04 sample
monitors from the Complainant premises for the purpose of conducting a Failure
Analysis to identify the cause of black spot on the Monitors. To ensure that
the Complainant is not put to any inconvenience OP-1 also gave replacement
monitors as a gesture of good will. The monitors panel was sent for the
failure analysis to be conducted by the original product manufacturer, LG
Korea. The failure analysis report clearly indicates that formation black spots
on the monitors were due to Fungus caused by humidity and improper customer
operation, condition / environment which rendered the monitors irreparable. The
OP-1 has mentioned in its version that the Monitors were sold to the OP-3 along
with three years advanced exchanged warranty. The OP3 should have passed on
the same warranty to its other dealers. The warranty provided by the OP-1 does
not cover any damage/ issue caused due to environment conditions, storage
conditions, accident etc as mentioned in the Damage Exclusion clause of NBD
(Next Business Day). The technical support personnel of the OP-1 has clearly
mentioned to the OP-2 that only in the event the present case came under the
NBD warranty, will OP-1 be liable to replace the monitors under warranty. The
failure analysis report provides for the cause of the black spot to be poor
shortage conditions of the customers. It is reiterated that when OP-1
dispatched the monitors to the OP-3, the monitors were in good working
condition and did not contain any defects in respect of manufacturing or
otherwise. Therefore, the OP-1 cannot be held responsible for the appearance of
the black spots on the monitor due to environmental conditions at Complainants premises,
this issue is not covered under the NBD warranty and therefore the OP-1 is
unable to replace the monitors under the NBD warranty.
4. Regarding parawise denial the OP-1 has submitted that the OP-2 is
not the Sales Representative of the OP-1 and the OP-2 purchased the monitors
from the OP-3 and sold the same to the Complainant. The OP-1 is the
manufacturer of the monitors who sold the same to the OP-3 in the month of
March 2008. The OP1 is unaware whether the Complainant faced problem with the monitors
since inception as the OP-1 was informed about the problem only on 02.12.2008.
It has been submitted by the OP-1 that the monitors were provided with three
years Advanced Exchange Next Business Day Warranty. As per the terms of NBD
warranty damaged due to environment conditions are not covered by the said
warranty the OP-1 is not in a position to replace the goods by a new one or to
refund the amount to the Complainant. The OP-1 has prayed for dismissal of
complaint with exemplary cost in the interest of justice and equity.
5. The OP-2 has contested the petition of complaint by filing very
cryptic written version wherein it has been stated by it that no cause of
action arose against the OP-2, which led the Complainant to prefer the instant
complaint. This complaint suffers from mis-joinder of parties and the OP-2 is
not liable for anything whatsoever relating to the claim of the Complainant.
The OP-2 has contended that it being the Sales Representative of the OP-1 get
order and used to supply the articles manufactured by the OP-1 to the
purchasers as per price list and all other documents and papers as he supplied
by the OP-1 to the purchasers. The OP-2 has no liability regarding
manufacturing defect as the articles are manufactured by the OP-1. No warranty
or guaranty has ever been issued or granted by the OP-2 but has been issued and
guaranteed by the OP-1. This OP on good
faith and bonafide belief to maintain the good will of its representation
requested the OP-1 for taking proper step to make good the articles supply or
to replace the same. The OP-2 has made all correspondences with the OP-1, which
it could not do as he has no liability but for the sake of good will of his
representation he has done it. The Complainant is not entitled to get any relief
from the OP-2 as prayed for in the complaint petition. According to the OP-2
the complaint is frivolous and harassing one, liable to be dismissed.
6. The OP-3 has contested the complaint petition by filing written
version wherein it is stated that no cause of action arose against it which led
the Complainant to prefer a complaint before this Commission. The OP-3 is not liable for anything
whatsoever relating to the claim of the Complainant. This OP inspected the
impugned DELL Monitors in question only once and expressed the opinion and as
such this Act cannot make this OP liable for anything whatsoever. The OP-3 has
emphatically denied the entire allegation made in the complaint petition. According to the OP-3 the complaint should
be dismissed with cost.
DECISION
WITH REASONS 

 

   

 

At the very outset it is
to be adjudicated that-
a)     
Whether
the Complainant is a consumer under the
Consumer Protect Act, 1986
.
b)     
Whether
this complaint is maintainable before this Commission or not.
c)     
Whether
the Complainant is entitled to get any compensation or not.
7. Now we are to discuss the point nos-a)
and b) jointly. Admittedly the Complainant purchased some desktops and monitors
from the OP-2 and the said products were manufactured by the OP-1. Moreover the
OP-2 purchased the said article from the OP-3. Further admitted fact is that
the Complainant purchased the said article against requisite payment of
consideration in full and the allegation of the Complainant is that the said
monitors became defective almost since its installation. Four new monitors have
replaced the Complainant made several correspondences with the OPs, but though
four monitors, but the balance 56 monitors are lying as used and defective
condition. The Complainant filed this complaint praying for direction upon the
OPs either to replace the defective monitors with new one or to refund of the
entire cost of the 56 monitors along with interest, compensation and
litigation. We have noticed that the Complainant filed this complaint alleging
deficiency in service against the OPs and for this reason the complaint is
maintainable and the Complainant is a consumer within the definition of the
Consumer as per the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
. Thus the point nos- (a)
and (b) are disposed of in favour of the Complainant.
8.
The Complainant and the OPs have filed evidence on affidavit and all the
parties were cross-examined, both parties filed brief notes of argument and
written notes of arguments in support of their respective contentions. We have
carefully perused the above-mentioned items; documents and papers filed by the
parties and heard the arguments advanced by the parties at length. It is seen
by us that the complainant is a school-Shree Jain Vidyalaya. As per the
Complainant i.e. Sri Parashmal Kankaria, being the secretary of the said
Vidyalaya has adduced evidence, which has stated that his Vidyalaya is a
non-profitable and charitable organization and a society registered under the
Registration of Society Act
XXI of 1860 having registration no-1066/192 of
1941-42. Though the OP-1 has alleged that the Complainants school is providing
education for commercial purpose, but in the reply no-4 of the OP-1, it has
stated that it did not file any document or any evidence to show that the said
Vidyalaya is providing education for commercial purpose. So the OP-1 though
alleged, but has failed to prove the said allegation by adducing any cogent
document in support of its contention. Therefore it is clear that the Complainant
being a consumer of the OPs has filed this complaint because it purchased
monitors and desktops from the OP-1 through the OP-2 against payment of
consideration and as those monitors suffered from defects since its
installation the Complainant prayed for either replacement or refund of the
amount, but the OPs did not pay any heed to its requests. Then the Complainant
being compelled approached before this Commission alleging deficiency in
service and unfair trade practice against the OPs. For this reason the
complaint is maintainable before this Commission
u/s 17
of the Consumer
Protection Act, 1986. This complaint has been filed within the territorial and
pecuniary jurisdictions of this Commission.
9.
Admittedly for the purpose of betterment of the students of the school, the
school has decided to purchase 30 dell desktops computers along with 30 17-inch
LCD monitors of Dell made and approached the OP-2, who according to the
complainant is the sales representative of the OP-1 in the month of July, 2008.
The OP-2 issued one offer and rate chart as cost of those computers and LCD
monitors through their letter dated 29.07.2008. as per the said offer letter of
the complainant purchased 30 dell desktops and 30 LCD 17 inch monitors on
07.08.2008 against payment of Rs.10,54,560/-. The complainant-school also
exchanged 30 existing monitors of dell made with the OP-2 and thereby the
school obtained 60 monitors. The OPs provided three years warranty for all the
purchased computers and LCD monitors. The OP-2 installed all the desktops and
monitors at the school, but the allegation of the complainant is that since its
installation 60 monitors became defective along with several spots on the
screen of those 60 LCD monitors of Dell made. According to the Complainant all
the monitors are almost in a bad condition and therefore lying in an unused
condition. Admittedly the defects in all the LCD monitors were occurred within
the warranty period and thus the Complainant immediately complained before the
OP-2 for removal of the defects since 02.12.2008. We have noticed that after
receipt of the complaint from the Complainant the OP-2 and even the OP-3
started regular correspondences with the OP-1, the manufacturer of the goods
through e-mail, but to no effect. The
OP-2 and 3 visited the school of the Complainant and inspected those defective
monitors and opined that the same were defective. One service engineer namely
Sri Atanu Roy inspected those monitors on 03.12.2008 and found lots of black
spots in the LCD monitor screen. Thereafter
the OP-2 requested the OP-1 through e-mail on 04.12.2008 for replacement of all
60 monitors and their expert engineer or mechanic made further request for
inspection of the goods. After several persuasions the OP-1 send their mechanic
for replacement of only four LCD monitors out of 60 on 23.12.2008 but did not
replace rest defective monitors inspite of repeated requests. The Complainant
wrote letter on 24.01.2009 to all the OPs requesting them to replace all the
rest defective monitors on or before 10.02.2009, but to effect. Admittedly the
OP-2 requested the OP-1 in this context because the students were suffering. In
reply the OP-1 stated that after examination of the monitor panels by their
engineer it was found that due to fungus caused by humidity and improper
customer operation condition/environment, which rendered the monitors
irreparable.
10.
In the evidence on affidavit the OP-2 has stated that they are nothing but a
sales representative of the OP-1 who use to sale the articles manufacture by
the OP-1 and deliver the same to the purchaser. It has been further stated by
the OP-2 that in connection with the sell of the articles the OP-1 issued all
the price list and other relevant papers and documents for such sale and they
are only entitled to get commission on such sale but nothing else. The OP-2 has
mentioned as the purchased articles were manufactured by the OP-1, OP-1 is
solely responsible about such manufacturing defects and OP-1 is bound to remove
the defects of the articles supplied to the complainant and the OP-1 is not
connected with manufacturing of the product and hence the Complainant is not
entitled to claim any amount from the OP-2. We have noticed that the proprietor
of M/s. ACC Infotech-OP-2 handed over one letter to the Complainant
(annexure-D) wherein it is stated that the articles carry three years onsite
warranty by Principal Company. On the other hand the OP-1 in its evidence on
affidavit has stated that it sold the monitors to the OP-3 under the next
business day warranty. The OP-3 should have passed on the same warranty to its
other dealers and or customers. The warranty provided by the OP-1 does not
cover any damage caused due to environment conditions storage conditions,
accident etc as mentioned in the damage exclusions clause of the NBD document. The
FA report provides for the cause of the black spots to be poor storage
conditions of the customer and while the OP-1 dispatched the monitors to the
OP-3 the same were in good working condition and did not contain any defects
either manufacturing or otherwise, so the OP-1 cannot be held liable for the
appearance of black spots on the monitors due to environmental conditions at
customers premises and as the issue is not covered under the NBD warranty,
therefore the OP-1 is unable to replace the monitors under NBD warranty. In
this respect we are to say that the OP-1 could not prove by producing any
document that while the products were dispatched to the OP-3, same were in good
working condition and it has also failed to prove that the articles became
defective while the same were under the possession of the Complainant. In
respect of the evidence of the OP-2 we are to say that why the NBD warranty did
not provide to the Complainant at the time of delivery of the article and why
the OP-2 supplied the warranty in its letterhead. As the Complainant purchased
the monitors from the OP-2 directly, it is the OP-1 who is liable to answer
whether there was actually any NBD warranty or not. In this respect there is no
whisper in their evidence. Admittedly the OP-2 supplied the goods to the
Complainant against payment of consideration and the Complainant paid the
entire amount to the OP-2. So now the OP-2 is under obligation that where is
the said warranty as issued by the OP-1 and as the Complainant was not supplied
with the same, the Complainant is entitled to get replacement of the defective
monitors or refund of the cost of the said goods. The monitors got damage, but
at what end it got the damage the OPs could not prove the same. Therefore in
our view the OP-2 shall take initiative with the OP-1 to replace the defective
monitors of the Complainant otherwise to refund the entire cost of the article.
As the OP-2 is the sales representative of the OP-1 the OP-1 also shall take steps
in respect of replacement of rest of the defective monitors or to refund the
entire cost of the goods to the Complainant. As the OP-2 purchased the said
article from the OP-3, the OP-3 is also liable to take initiative in the
above-mentioned respect, as it cannot be said that the monitors did not get
damage while it was under the custody of the OP-3. It is seen by us that the
Complainant being a school requested the OPs on several occasions to rectify
the defects or replace the goods by a new one or refund the cost of the article;
the OPs specially the OP-1 did not pay any heed to such request of the
Complainant for a long period. Thereafter though the OP-1 replaced only four
monitors, but in respect of the rest the OP-1 remained silent and did not bother
to take any initiative and such inaction compelled the Complainant to approach
before the Court of Law and simultaneously the OP-2s action suffers from
deficiency in service as it did not hand over the actual warranty card or
document to the Complainant and which it had given to the purchaser does not
carry any value as it was written in its letter head, which is an example of
unfair trade practice on behalf of the OP-2. Due to such deficiency in service
and unfair trade practice on the parts of the OP-1 and 2, the Complainant is
entitled to get compensation and litigation cost from the OP-1 and 2.
ORDERING
PORTION
11.
Going by the foregoing discussion hence it is ordered that the complaint be
allowed on contest with cost. The OP-1 and 2 shall pay a sum of Rs.5,000/-
towards compensation due to harassment and mental agony as well as loss of
reputation of the school either jointly or severally to the Complainant and the
OP-1 and 2 shall also pay litigation cost of Rs.3,000/- to the Complainant
either jointly or severally. The OP-1 and 2 shall take steps for replacement of
the rest defective monitors of the Complainants or refund the entire cost of
the defective monitors for a sum of Rs.10,54,560/- along with interest @6% p.a. to the Complainant within 45 days
from the date of this judgment. In case of refund of the cost of the defective
monitors the Complainant shall returned all the items to the said party from
which the school purchased it. The OP-1
and 2 shall pay the above-mentioned amounts to the Complainant as per direction
mentioned above within 45 days from the date of this judgment; in default the
total amount shall carry interest @8% p.a. for the default period. Point no (c)
is thus disposed of in favour of the Complainant.
Sri. Shankar Coari.
Smt. Silpi Majumder.
